title: Lesson 5 - Initial Use Cases: Customer 360, Real-Time Personalization, and Next Best Action
description: Identify initial use cases for Data 360, covering the highest-value starting patterns (Customer 360 unified profiles, real-time personalization, and next best action).

questions.question: A retailer wants to recommend products on its website based on a shopper's recent browsing and cart events within the same session. Which Data 360 capability set best fits?
options: Real-time identity resolution, real-time calculated insights, and real-time actions
A monthly calculated insight and a dashboard
questions.explanation: In-session personalization needs real-time identity resolution to merge devices, real-time insights to compute scores, and real-time actions to respond. Batch segmentation is the strongest distractor but it is far too slow for in-session decisions.

questions.question: A service team wants to see the full cross-channel history of a customer on the service console record. Which initial use case is this?
options: A calculated insight on lifetime value
A unified Customer 360 profile surfaced in the console
Zero Copy federation of a warehouse
questions.explanation: Showing unified cross-channel history to an agent is the Customer 360 profile use case. A lifetime value insight is a component you could add, but it is not the core of the console view.

questions.question: Which prerequisite most often blocks an initial use case from working?
options: The org has too many users
The unifying entity is not mapped and unified, so the profile does not exist
The data is stored in a data lake
The segment has too few members
questions.explanation: Use cases built on profiles or segments require the entity, Individual or Account, to be mapped to the Customer 360 Data Model and unified. Data location does not block Data 360, which handles lakes through federation.
